title: Long-Distance Travel Allowance for Standing Referrals (Primary Care Provider Assignment)
content:
**Schedule — travel visits on a standing referral, Primary Care Provider Assignment.**

Travel visits are added to a standing referral's allowance for members who travel far for care, before the standing-referral visit ceiling is applied. The measure is the longest one-way distance of the member's completed medical-appointment transportation legs on record under **Non-Emergency Medical Transportation** — legs recorded as completed, with the trip purpose medical appointment, compared by their one-way miles. Every such leg on record counts, whatever its date.

| Longest completed medical-appointment leg (one-way miles) | Travel visits added |
|---|---|
| 30.0 or more (the far distance) | 4 (the larger travel allowance) |
| At least 15.0 but less than 30.0 (the middle distance) | 2 (the smaller travel allowance) |
| Less than 15.0, or no such leg | 0 |

**Both sides of each band (hypothetical longest legs)**

| Longest leg | Travel visits |
|---|---|
| 30.0 miles | 4 |
| 29.9 miles | 2 |
| 15.0 miles | 2 |
| 14.9 miles | 0 |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A member's completed medical-appointment legs on record measure 12.4, 31.2 and 18.0 miles one way. The longest is 31.2 miles, at least the far distance of 30.0, so 4 travel visits are added. A leg of 40.0 miles to a pharmacy or a food bank is not a medical-appointment leg and is not measured.
